Elena — thanks for the note and the redlines.

Short answer up front: we are willing to negotiate a middle path that balances customer control with Redwood's ability to manage claims efficiently. Practically that means:

- Notice: Customer gives prompt written notice and reasonably cooperates.
- Evidence: Redwood asks for the claim notice, relevant prompt examples (redacted), and system logs related to the alleged output; we commit to limiting requests to items reasonably necessary to evaluate the claim.
- Defense control: For third-party IP claims alleging infringement of a third party's IP by Redwood's model or service, Redwood requests primary defense control with privilege for Redwood counsel; for claims arising solely from customer-provided content or fine-tuning data, customer control is reasonable.
- Insurance / escrow: We can accept a standard insurance-offset clause and are open to discussing escrow for high-risk regulatory customers, but not as a general requirement.

I'll loop in Kim (legal) for clean language — Ben, can you confirm that this aligns with the commercial terms we discussed on the call? I propose a 30-minute call next week with Nimble counsel to move toward a one-page compromise.

Thanks,

Elena / team — Kim from Redwood Legal. Thanks for flagging — attached are two items: (1) a clean redline of the indemnity section (Redwood_evidence_checklist.xlsx) and (2) a short evidence checklist we think is reasonable to limit scope. High-level notes below.

1) Defense control: Redwood proposes primary defense control for IP claims that allege infringement by Redwood's models or by our hosted service, subject to (a) Redwood conducting the defense in good faith and (b) Redwood providing periodic updates. If Nimble demonstrates the claim solely arises from Nimble-provided training data or customer prompts, Nimble may assume control.

2) Evidence scope: We will limit requests to: the claim notice, a small set of exemplar prompts/responses (up to 10, redacted for PHI), server logs showing request timestamps and model/version, and any customer-provided data that is specifically implicated. We will not request production of customer product roadmaps or unrelated PII.

3) Insurance / offset: We accept an insurance-offset mechanic ( insurer payment reduces indemnity amount ) but cannot accept automatic invoice offsets without mutual written agreement.

4) Timing: Redwood requests a 30-day window to evaluate and propose a defense plan after notice is received; if Nimble needs to take interim steps, the parties will coordinate.

If Nimble signs off on the checklist, we will incorporate the redlines into an updated order form and circulate.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Dylan — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few areas Nimble counsel cannot accept as written: 

- Primary defense control is a hard sell for us; our Board requires customer ability to assume defense on high‑exposure claims and control who signs settlement terms that impact our users. We can accept Redwood participating in the defense (co-counsel) but not sole control for core IP allegations.
- The 10-example limit is helpful but we need stronger guarantees on PHI handling and a binding process for redaction verification.
- We asked procurement to run a parallel review of the escrow/insurance requirement — they will push for an escrow-trigger tied to remediation funds if a claim materially impacts customers.

We are available for a call Wednesday 18th 09:00 PT or Thursday 19th 11:00 PT. Please confirm which slot works and we will send a calendar invite; we'll also include a short countertrack with redline highlights (nimble-counsel-countertrack.docx).

Taylor / Elena / Samir — thanks. We hear the concerns and want to avoid scope creep that will stall signing. Proposal to break forward:

1) Stand-up a 30-minute legal-to-legal call Thursday 19th at 11:00 PT (if that still works) — agenda: defense control boundary, evidence redaction process, escrow trigger thresholds.
2) For the order form in the interim, agree to compromise language: Redwood primary defense with an explicit carve for claims demonstrably arising only from Nimble-provided content (customer assumes defense), and an approval right for Nimble on any settlement that imposes ongoing obligations on Nimble or its users.
3) Agree to a short PHI handling protocol (Kim will circulate a two-line binding assurance and a handshake process for redaction verification).
4) Escrow: Redwood will accept a deal-specific escrow trigger for material incidents (threshold: customer-reported outage or regulatory filing) for enterprise deals only — not standard for all orders.

If we can get provisional agreement on items 2 and 3, Redwood will update the order form and circulate a tracked copy for execution. Ben will follow up on commercial margin implications of the escrow ask.

Can you confirm the call time and whether the provisional approach is acceptable so we can avoid a long redline loop?
